newsitem.title: NORWAY: Bergesen bullish on nearby tanker outlook.
newsitem.headline: Bergesen bullish on nearby tanker outlook.

text.p: Norway's largest shipping company Bergesen ASA said on Thursday it had a positive view on the tanker market and expected further improvement in the sector in the next two years.
But in the longer-term, developments in tankers could be problematic, said Jan Haakon Pettersen, Bergesen's head of operations.
"Our view is for continued positive development for the next couple of years compared with three-quarters of a year ago," Pettersen said.
"We will see periods of high rates, which will be followed by weaker periods. But the timing between good periods will become shorter and shorter."

Pettersen said warnings of increasing oil production near consumers, such as in the North Sea and West Africa, did not change the positive outlook. Very large crude carriers (VLCCs) form a large part of the cargo traffic from such areas, he said.
Also, he said, if Suezmax rates rise to 20-25 points over VLCC rates it is more economic for operators to combine two Suexmax vessels to a single VLCC.

"At the end of last week we had some very good rates, especially from West Africa to the U.S. Gulf," he said, pointing to 1973-built Berge Prince, which was fixed at World Scale 72.5, or the equivalent of $35,000 per day.
Developments in the time charter sector also were pointing in the right direction. One to two years ago daily time charter rates were in the low $20,000s, but were now around $30,000, Pettersen said.
Pettersen said the longer-term outlook was clouded by unused capacity and high investment capital to build new vessels.
"The biggest danger in shipping is spare capacity and shipowners or speculators eager to invest in newbuildings," he said.
